name: Client Workshop
description: Client design and requirements workshops, kickoffs, scoping and estimation reviews, and reviews of workshop minutes or open points

sections.title: Session Overview
sections.instruction: Summarize the client, workstream, products and processes covered, whether the client was present or it was an internal Murex session, what was demoed, and which agenda topics were deferred to other sessions. Cover the whole session from start to end

sections.title: Client Current Process
sections.instruction: List how the client works today as described in the meeting: systems used, manual steps, workarounds, spreadsheets and pain points, naming the region, desk or team each applies to

sections.title: Requirements & Murex Fit
sections.instruction: One row per requirement or topic. Give who raised it, how strongly the client needs it (must-have, nice-to-have, not used today) only when stated, what Murex showed or proposed, and classify the fit as standard, configuration, workaround or gap

sections.title: Scope, Phasing & Effort
sections.instruction: List items whose scope or phase was stated or changed, the basis cited (SOW, change request, client request), and any effort or cost figure exactly as stated (man-days, amounts, fixed cost or T&M). Do not compute totals that were not said. Write man-days where the transcript says Mondays or mandis in an effort context

sections.title: Decisions & Agreements
sections.instruction: List only points both sides agreed, the client explicitly confirmed, or the team agreed to take as its position, and who confirmed each. Do not list explanations of how Murex works by default

sections.title: Open Questions & Pending Inputs
sections.instruction: List unresolved questions, documents, data or confirmations still needed, and changes made to the open-points register (closed, merged, re-owned, reworded), saying whether the client or Murex owes each item

sections.title: Risks & Dependencies
sections.instruction: List risks and concerns raised, including estimate uncertainty, dependencies on other workstreams, systems, sessions or decommissioning, and follow-up sessions scheduled

sections.title: Action Items
sections.instruction: List tasks someone committed to, saying for each whether the owner is on the Client or Murex side. Use the owner's name as spoken in the conversation, write Unassigned when no owner is named, never use speaker labels or descriptions of the speaker, and never merge two people into one owner. Write Not specified when no due date was given, leave out meeting logistics such as sending a link, and always add the reference transcript segment and timestamp
